page: Amazon Web Services m7i-flex.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 128 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which accelerate deep learning and cryptographic workloads. In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 2023.0 in Geekbench single-core tests and achieving 32.42 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core performance is solid, with a Passmark CPU score of 47,332.26 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU throughput of 32,413.77.

Memory performance is supported by high-speed DDR5, showing a cached small-block read bandwidth of 2,436.4 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read bandwidth of 170.39 GB/sec. The instance excels in static web serving throughput at 48.18 GB/sec and handles text processing and image processing efficiently. For language model workloads, the instance manages small-model (135M) text generation at a strong rate of 332.68 tokens/sec, though performance drops to a weak 2.67 tokens/sec for text generation on large (70B) models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m7i-flex family offers a resource-dense profile for general-purpose workloads that do not require continuous maximum CPU utilization. It delivers a balanced ratio of compute to memory without the added cost of bundled local NVMe storage. This makes the m7i-flex.8xlarge highly suitable for applications such as web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate machine learning inference tasks that leverage CPU-based matrix acceleration.
